title: Some books we’re reading this summer 2026
gist: a16z crypto's staff summer-reading roundup is mostly personal literary picks with little direct investing content, but a handful of entries explicitly use book frameworks to reason about crypto, AI, energy constraints, and competitive moats.

insights.claim: Apple spent over a decade and substantial resources training Chinese manufacturers to build its products to stringent precision requirements, a deliberate capability-transfer effort rather than an accident, which built the manufacturing base that now underpins China's electronics dominance.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Reshoring or de-risking supply chains away from China is structurally harder than it looks because the manufacturing capability was purpose-built over years, not incidental.
insights.quote: Apple spent over a decade and many resources to train firms in China to build Apple products, with stringent requirements and high precision.
insights.locator: Dan Boneh, research — Apple in China by Patrick McGee

insights.claim: The recorded music industry's history shows technology repeatedly destroying the prevailing business model in succession (piracy, then iTunes, then YouTube, then streaming), with each new equilibrium proving temporary rather than final.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Investors should treat any incumbent industry's current business model, including today's crypto and finance structures, as a temporary equilibrium likely to be disrupted again rather than a stable end-state.
insights.quote: the music industry’s current model as just another temporary equilibrium waiting to be disrupted
insights.locator: Drew Coffman, editorial — How Music Got Free by Stephen Witt

insights.claim: A five-century history of energy transitions (wood to coal to oil to electricity to nuclear/renewables) suggests progress has come as much from scaling capacity as from fundamental breakthroughs, a pattern now repeating as AI compute demand revives interest in nuclear power and forces grid reinvestment.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Investors in AI infrastructure should watch energy and grid capacity (especially nuclear) as the binding constraint on the next computing era, not just chip or algorithm progress.
insights.quote: The constraint on this next computing era may be joules rather than algorithms, a challenge we’ve navigated before.
insights.locator: Aiden Slavin, policy — Energy by Richard Rhodes

themes.theme: Crypto framed through institutional economics and financial theory

insights.claim: Acemoglu and Robinson's thesis that inclusive institutions drive prosperity while extractive ones cause stagnation is used explicitly as a lens for evaluating blockchain protocols, framing decentralized protocols as attempts to hard-code inclusive institutions through open access and code-enforced rules rather than gatekeepers.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating a protocol's durability should assess it on institutional-quality criteria (capture risk, insider concentration, gatekeeping) rather than tokenomics alone, since some ecosystems thrive while others get captured by insiders.
insights.quote: Decentralized protocols are essentially an attempt to hard-code inclusive institutions: open access, no gatekeepers, rules enforced by code rather than by whoever’s in power.
insights.locator: Kira Song, finance — Why Nations Fail by Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson

insights.claim: Donald MacKenzie's account of how academic financial models don't just describe markets but actively reshape them once adopted is flagged as newly relevant given recent traditional-finance (TradFi) interest in crypto.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: As institutional capital and its risk/pricing models flow into crypto, the models themselves may restructure crypto market behavior rather than merely observe it — worth tracking which TradFi models get imported and how they change price formation.
insights.quote: What happens when theories stop describing the world and start changing it?
insights.locator: Tim Sullivan, editorial — An Engine, Not a Camera by Donald MacKenzie

insights.claim: A memoir about a punk band's mainstream success draws an explicit parallel to how countercultures that go mainstream lose their original meaning, citing jazz, hip-hop, streetwear, and open source software alongside crypto's own trajectory toward mainstream adoption.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: As crypto goes mainstream, expect the same identity and authenticity tension seen in other subcultures-turned-industries — a signal to watch for backlash or fragmentation among early adherents as adoption widens.
insights.quote: A similar arc can be traced across jazz, abstract art, hip-hop, skateboarding, streetwear, open source software, and, relevantly for this audience, crypto.
insights.locator: Robert Hackett, editorial — Fahrenheit-182: A Memoir by Mark Hoppus

themes.theme: Formal verification as AI and crypto infrastructure

insights.claim: Lean, a machine-checkable proof-assistant language launched by Leonardo de Moura in 2013, has expanded from formalizing pure mathematics into cryptography, software security, and economics, and is now positioned as a critical complement to generative AI because it gives AI models a language to reason in and a trusted system to verify or reject AI-generated proofs.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Formal-verification tooling like Lean is becoming infrastructure for trustworthy AI outputs in math, code, and crypto — a technology category worth tracking as AI-generated proofs and code increasingly need independent, machine-checkable verification.
insights.quote: Lean at once turns proof logic into a machine language that AI models can reason in more easily, and provides a trusted system to verify (or reject) conclusions when AI models try to “prove” in ways that are difficult for humans to understand.
insights.locator: Scott Duke Kominers, research — The Proof in the Code by Kevin Hartnett

insights.claim: Edward Thorp's application of systematic, mathematical methods first to beating casino blackjack and then to Wall Street investing is cited as capturing the same builder mindset of using pure logic to disrupt rigged, legacy systems that the reviewer sees at work in crypto today.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Crypto builders' self-image of disrupting entrenched, opaque financial systems via systematic edge (in the mold of Thorp) is a framing worth watching as it shapes product strategy and market rhetoric.
insights.quote: using pure logic to disrupt rigged, legacy systems, which completely captures the exact same builder mindset we see in crypto today
insights.locator: Benjamin Wu, talent — A Man for All Markets by Edward O. Thorp

insights.claim: Former Samsung Electronics chairman Oh-Hyun Kwon's 'Super Gap' framework argues durable competitive advantage requires a lead wide enough that competitors cannot even consider challenging it, built across four pillars — leader, organization, strategy, and talent — spanning technology, systems, and culture, not technology alone.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: A useful diligence lens for assessing whether a portfolio company's moat (including in semiconductors or crypto infrastructure) is a true structural gap versus a temporary technical lead.
insights.quote: “The Super Gap” means a gap so wide that competitors cannot even think about challenging you.
insights.locator: SungMo Park, go-to-market — The Super Gap by Oh-Hyun Kwon

themes.theme: AI and the future of work

insights.claim: A 1948 philosophical argument that leisure is a contemplative stance toward reality, not idleness, is invoked as newly relevant to the AI era, framing the open question as what human 'doing' was ever for once AI absorbs most economically productive tasks.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: As AI automates execution and output, human economic value may shift toward judgment, taste, and contemplative work rather than task throughput — relevant to which human skills retain a wage premium.
insights.quote: As AI absorbs more of the doing, the open question becomes what the doing was ever for.
insights.locator: Conner Lyons Brown, tech ops — Leisure: The Basis of Culture by Josef Pieper
